title: fix(ui): give Systems its own sidebar header
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Systems shows the Sessions header (owner picker, session filter, new session) above its device list, and the agent avatar does not leave Systems.

## User Impact

Systems has its own header with only the collapse control; the device search and filter stay. The agent avatar returns to the last session.

## Why This Change Was Made

A page that brings its own sidebar list gets its own title header, and the avatar no longer treats it as the open Sessions list.

## Evidence

Screenshots come from the Control UI mock at the end of the series, so the after image can show later parts too.

Systems before and after (left: main, right: after):

![Systems before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/093c86db-1673-40f5-b87b-de203e3d35a6)

- `pnpm tsgo:ui` passes at this PR's head.
- The unit tests of the files this PR touches pass at its head; the full UI unit suite passes at the end of the series (one failure also on main: a Workboard German relative-time string, "vor 1min", from the local ICU).
- Local autoreview (Codex) over the whole series; its three findings are fixed in this series.
- The full UI e2e suite was not run locally.

Side rail series, part 12 of 16. Stacked on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199832; review only this PR's commits.

### Approved navigation-stack JS budget

Vyctor approved the measured JavaScript byte cost for this navigation stack. These cumulative measurements compare this layer with paired main base `1d82bed0a7fef79012c38ea7e6184911aba27e63`. Each cap equals the original main cap plus the measured delta, preserving existing headroom without adding another margin.

| Metric | Cumulative gzip delta | Cap |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Largest JS asset | +3,714 B | 576,154 B |
| Chat boot JS | +3,959 B | 1,329,539 B |
| New Session boot JS | +4,143 B | 820,775 B |

CSS ceilings, request counts, startup ceilings and gate logic are unchanged. Byte measurements are delivery-size evidence, not latency measurements.

Previously verified functional and integrated visual proof was reused where inputs are unchanged; the maintainer also exercised the integrated stack on a real Gateway.
